title: Rav Shalman
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Berakhot 39b has a reciter teaching before Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak. He asks his name. “Shalman,” he answers. Rav Nachman replies: “You are peace, and your teaching is complete, for you have made peace among the students.”
And he is mentioned in Bava Kamma 89a: Rav Shalman said, "Because there is ease for the household," and this refers to the words of Abaye.
And in Bava Batra 13b: Rav Shalman interpreted it as referring to a case where both are willing, and this refers to the words of Abaye.
In Menachot 29a, Rav Shalman cites the verse “to its base,” etc.
And at the end of the Rif he is called by the name Shalmon.

notes.text: The reciter’s name underlies the peace/complete wordplay. The Menachot phrase concerns the menorah’s base, not an anatomical thigh. Hyman does not identify which tractate’s Rif conclusion has Shalmon.

The directly inspected Berakhot 39b supports the reciter’s Shalman/shalom/shelemah wordplay, and Menachot 29a quotes the menorah’s base. The exact unspecified end-of-Rif Shalmon reading remains Hyman’s report; the Biblical parenthesis does not identify the sage with a Biblical namesake.
